name: Dionysius of Cyzicus
bio: Dionysius of Cyzicus is one of the epigrammatists whose short poems were gathered in the Greek Anthology. Paton's index of authors gives no date for the poet. Paton's index lists the poet among the writers of Meleager's Wreath, the Garland compiled about 100 BC.
This archive carries the 2 epigrams ascribed to the poet in the second volume of W. R. Paton's prose translation (Book VII: 78, 462).

poems.title: Book VII, 78: On Eratosthenes
poems.author: Dionysius of Cyzicus
poems.text: A mild old age, no darkening disease, put out thy light, Eratosthenes son of Aglaus, and, thy high studies over, thou sleepest the appointed sleep. Cyrene thy mother did not receive thee into the tombs of thy fathers, but thou art buried on this fringe of Proteus’ shore,' beloved even in a strange land.

poems.title: Book VII, 462
poems.author: Dionysius of Cyzicus
poems.text: Satyra with child and near her time has been taken by Hades. The earth of Sidon covers her, and Tyre her country bewails her.

poems.title: Peace in the End (Mackail)
poems.author: Dionysius of Cyzicus
poems.collection: Select Epigrams from the Greek Anthology (1890)
poems.text: A gentler old age and no dulling disease quenched thee, and thou didst fall asleep in the slumber to which all must come, O Eratosthenes, after pondering over high matters; nor did Cyrene where thou sawest the light receive thee within the tomb of thy fathers, O son of Aglaus; yet dear even in a foreign land art thou buried here, by the edge of the beach of Proteus.
